question: Plot Lorenz attractor in 2d using 5 different initial conditions distinguished in different colors

cells.why: New chain: the Lorenz attractor, five initial conditions, two dimensions, five colours. This turn sets up the model and integrator, runs all five trajectories at once, and checks three things before any plotting: that the step size is small enough that the numbers are the ODE's and not the integrator's, where in space the attractor actually lives, and when the five trajectories stop being distinguishable from each other — because that determines what the colours can honestly show.

cells.why: Last turn produced five nearby trajectories (x₀ = 1.00…1.04) and showed their separation from the first crossing 0.1, 1 and 10 at progressively earlier times — but that crossing table both understates the growth rate and says nothing about which time window the plot should cover. This turn measures the divergence rate properly (two-trajectory Lyapunov estimate plus a fit to the observed separations), and tests a set of five *widely spread* initial conditions for how long each transient takes to reach the attractor and how much of the attractor a given window of time covers, so the plotting window is chosen from the data rather than guessed.
cells.purpose: This turn measures the divergence rate properly (two-trajectory Lyapunov estimate plus a fit to the observed separations), and tests a set...

cells.why: Cell 6's diagnostics showed two things that must be fixed before any figure: the near-identical-pair separation slopes (0.11–0.16/time unit) were fitted over a saturating range and are far below the Lyapunov estimate, and one of the five "widely spread" ICs — (−8,−8,27), the unstable fixed point C− — needed 16.3 time units just to reach the attractor, so at T=20 that colour is nearly blank (2% coverage). This turn refits the separation growth honestly and screens a pool of candidate initial conditions for transient time, coverage and colour overlap, so the five plotted ICs are chosen on evidence rather than taste.

cells.why: Cell 7 screened candidate initial conditions and showed that the two unstable fixed points C± never move (arc length 0) while six candidates reach the attractor within t≈4; it also refit the separation growth in a non-saturating window (mean 0.079 /time unit — much smaller than the 0.856 from the renormalised two-trajectory method, a saturation artefact I will report as such). The colour-overlap diagnostic was defined but never called, so this turn fixes the five initial conditions, measures exactly how long their colours stay apart in the x–z projection, and measures how much of the attractor the union paints.

cells.why: Cell 8's headline number is an artefact: "last time a pair is still >2 apart" is 50.00 for every pair because two points on the attractor are usually far apart in x–z whatever their history. This turn replaces that statistic with an honest one — a memory-free baseline (one long run compared with itself 100 time units later) and the time each IC pair first reaches that baseline scale — so the report quotes a merge horizon that means something.

cells.why: The last cell did what it was meant to: it showed cell 8's "pair still >2 apart" number is degenerate — the same statistic applied to one trajectory compared with itself 100 time units later also hits the 50 ceiling — so the merge story rests on the colour-overlap counts, not on that number. Before writing the report I want the legibility of each colour measured properly: how much of the attractor a single colour paints, and how much the five share, at t≤2, 5, 10, 20, 50. That is the number the figure's panel split will rest on.

cells.why: The review's point stands: the only thing that settles whether five colours show the attractor is whether each colour actually traces both lobes, and I can test that from `Pc` without drawing. This cell runs that test numerically — per-colour first visit to the x>0 and x<0 wings, fraction of samples falling outside the cells the long run occupies — and records it against the open test, plus a corrected line for cell 9's pair count.
